name: Measurements untrusted
problem: A number recorded on uncommitted code, on a different case set, typed by hand, or copied into prose that goes stale looks like evidence but cannot be reproduced. Two numbers from different conditions get compared as if they were alike.
who_has_it: Anyone deciding from a result: reviewers, Joshua, the selection itself.
why_it_matters: A wrong number leads to the wrong default, and once people notice untrustworthy numbers they stop reading metrics and go back to reading code.
why_hard: Provenance needs discipline every single time, several agents edit the same working copy at once, and noise makes small differences look real.
existing_attempts: Experiment trackers (MLflow, Weights and Biases), CI artifacts, lab notebooks, statistical significance tests.

name: Simulated arm shows a false loss
problem: An arm that meters a deterministic stand-in for a model counts the calls a real model would make at no cost. It is recorded with an unknown model and cost, so the harness skips it as paid and the ranking rates a free rival cheaper than a cost that is merely unknown, reporting a loss that is not real.
who_has_it: Maintainers of a project whose evaluations run offline stand-ins beside paid model arms.
why_it_matters: A false loss sends a person to fix a selection that is right, and a skipped arm leaves its result stale.
why_hard: A missing price looks the same for a free stand-in and for a paid model whose price was not entered, so being free cannot be inferred from the cost alone; the arm has to declare itself.
existing_attempts: Listing the arm as paid in configuration, or recording a zero cost by hand.

name: One run decides a ranking
problem: An arm that is run again and again has several results on the same cases and the same code, and the ranking reads only the newest, so a lucky or unlucky last run decides which arm leads and a record of the repeats changes nothing.
who_has_it: Anyone whose selection rests on repeated runs of the arms: the check, the promotion and the cascade.
why_it_matters: A model-calling arm passes a different number of cases on each run, so the newest run alone picks the leader by noise, and a consumer's own metric that pools its repeats then disagrees with the library's check.
why_hard: Only runs of the same code on the same cases are repeats, so the pool has to leave out a run of other code and a run on uncommitted code, and one pooled result must still compare with an arm run once.
existing_attempts: A waiver on each disagreement naming the pending decision; a consumer's own pooling that the library's check does not see.
